methodology: Use the canonical Zaporizhzhia alert episodes and canonical strict explosion results without rebuilding either dataset.
Exclude every episode already in the canonical strict explosion numerator before air-defense classification.

Require explicit Zaporizhzhia city attribution, explicit current air-defense action, and message/event timing inside the canonical episode. No blanket historical +/-5, +/-10, or +30 minute tolerance is applied.

Check repository-local research/source material first. The repository does not contain a full historical Zaporizhzhia raw Telegram export, so the pilot then used targeted indexed public media/Telegram searches for exact-city PПО formulations.
Deduplicate at alert-episode level: one episode contributes at most one air-defense numerator.
Because source discovery was pilot-level rather than a complete archive scan, strict positives below are a confirmed lower bound, not a claim that every historical PПО message was found.

workload.candidate_rate_warning: Pilot source discovery is not archive-exhaustive, so this density is a lower-bound workload observation and should not be multiplied mechanically across cities.
most_common_ambiguities: same alert episode already in strict explosion numerator
publication/post time vs actual event time
retrospective PПО summaries that cannot identify one episode
workload.rules_regex_plus_targeted_review_assessm: Technically feasible. The alert list can be excluded/matched automatically; manual effort is concentrated in a small candidate set, not in all 2196 eligible alerts.
workload.main_bottleneck: Completeness and timestamp quality of historical raw/source archives, especially Telegram, plus reliable city-vs-oblast attribution. Alert-episode volume itself is not the main bottleneck.
workload.recommendation_for_other_cities: Use raw historical exports where available, regex/rules for explicit PПО + exact-city terms, automatic exclusion of existing strict explosions, automatic episode-time join, then targeted review only for boundary/city-attribution cases.
